design.shape: Schedule trigger fans out to two Google data branches, each branch aggregates to a single item and is sorted by its own specialist agent, a Merge node in chooseBranch/waitForAll mode synchronises the branches, then a third agent composes the HTML dashboard which is delivered by Gmail.
agents: Email Triage Agent - buckets last-24h mail into ACTION REQUIRED / WAITING ON REPLY / FYI / NOISE and emits a TOP3 line
Calendar Agent - builds today's timeline, flags OVERLAPS, largest FREE block and PREP items
Briefing Editor Agent - merges both reports into a self-contained HTML dashboard
design.sharedSubNode: One OpenAI chat model sub-node (Briefing Model) serves all three agents via ai_languageModel
notes: No credentials key is emitted on any node, so every credential selector is empty in the n8n editor.
alwaysOutputData is set on the Gmail read and Google Calendar read nodes so a zero-email or zero-event day still reaches the agents.
Briefing Editor Agent reads the two upstream agent reports with $("Node Name").first().json.output; the Merge node exists only as a wait-for-all barrier.
The Gmail send expression strips markdown code fences from the model output before using it as the HTML body.
sendTo on the delivery node uses the session-provided user address etienne@etiennelescot.fr (the user's own inbox); no credential or secret was invented.

friction.what: Bash heredoc could not write the workflow file
friction.detail: cat > file <<'EOF' with the full .workflow.ts body failed with "unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote". Fell back to the Write tool, which succeeded on the first try.

friction.what: Bundled schema is shallow on collection parameters
friction.detail: skills node-info gmail types the message:getAll 'filters' parameter as any[] and skills node-schema gmail does not expand it at all. Had to read node_modules/@n8n-as-code/skills/dist/assets/n8n-nodes-technical.json directly to get the real option names (receivedAfter, readStatus, q, sender, labelIds, includeSpamTrash).
friction.impact: four extra ontology probes before authoring

friction.what: Ontology probing needed trial and error
friction.detail: n8n-nodes-technical.json is keyed as { nodes: { <shortName>: { schema: { properties: [...] } } } }, not an array; the first probe threw TypeError: nodes.find is not a function.

Toolchain message, verbatim: "Validated against the bundled schema only (native MCP level 0 - discouraged, the instance may differ). Connect the instance MCP for instance-exact validation: n8nac native-mcp configure --level 1." The level was NOT changed, per the agent contract that forbids the builder from running native-mcp configure.
friction.impact: workflow is validated against bundled schemas and the post-push fetch only, not against the live instance node definitions

friction.detail: workflow credential-required Y2JEWHYGKsU9xhQ0 --json returned [] and exited 0, although four nodes (two Gmail, one Google Calendar, one OpenAI chat model) deliberately have empty credential slots. It appears to report only declared-but-unresolvable credentials, not omitted ones, so it cannot be used to confirm that the slots are empty.
friction.impact: empty-slot state was confirmed by reading the pushed workflow file instead

friction.detail: The workflowsPath returned by env status --json pointed at a directory that had not been created yet; mkdir -p was required before writing the first workflow.

The push round-trip regenerated the file with server-assigned node ids, workflow id, settings { executionOrder: 'v1', availableInMCP: true } and a regenerated <workflow-map> header. Expected behaviour, noted so the diff is not mistaken for drift.
